works.name: Castillo de Palos de la Frontera

past: An older settlement grew into a town in Roman times. Its main routes survive, with irregular medieval lanes and plots shaped by the ground.
Walled.
A great fire burned 8 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The duke planted a “New Town” across the river: one straight street of equal plots. It never prospered on its own, and the council bought it out a generation later.
A great fire burned 13 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit runs wide of the old; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line; 17 houses were built into what was left of it.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the eastern side; 0 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
A great fire burned 19 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Cuervovilla
past: The bishop's cathedral and its burg stood on the dry rise; below, the count founded a merchants' town on the waterfront. For a generation they had two councils, then one. Canals — fleets — were dug from the harbour into the merchant quarter, so that lighters could unload at the warehouse doors.
Walled.
The Dominicans were given ground by the wall for their friary.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.

places.name: Guadalrey
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The ford was bridged in stone.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 60% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread.
7 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.

places.name: La Rábida
past: Farms and an alehouse about a green where the roads meet; a weekly market was granted in its second age.
Walled.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 94% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 50 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the southern side; 15 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.

places.name: Vado de Pardo
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
Granted a charter for a weekly market; the green was paved as a market place.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 60% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line; 2 houses were built into what was left of it.
A great fire burned 27 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
